evidence: Draft judged: "One reason might have been that I was sober when I did that, and didn't feel that susceptible to hypnosis. But I think a bigger reason is trust and precision." It sits once, verbatim, in CONTEXT.txt under "Why doing it myself worked better for me". Compared word by word with SOURCE.txt: his published guide ("Maybe part of that was state-dependent: I was sober and didn't feel especially suggestible. The larger issue was trust and precision.") and the replaced words ("I was sober at the session and didn't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision."). It does what the_change says: two sentences, Emulate's lead-ins, ending on his "trust and precision", with the hedge put back ("might have been" for "was", his "Maybe part of that"). Kept: being sober and not feeling suggestible as a possible partial reason, trust and precision as the larger one, in his order and with the same ranking. Who does what is unchanged (all first person, no one added). "when I did that" has the professional session as its antecedent ("the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist", the sentence before it); that is the only reading in which sobriety explains the weaker result, and his source says "at the session". No claim, person, number or condition is added. Small drifts I checked and accept: (1) "I think" is a hedge his flat "The larger issue was" lacks, so the second claim is a little softer than his; it is the same ranking claim (the replaced words already hedged it from the other side with "I suspect that's not even the main reason"), it matches the section's tentative voice ("seems far more useful", "might have been"), and it adds no claim, so I judge it a voice difference, not a change of position, but the card should let him see it. (2) "a bigger reason is" for "the larger issue was" (reason for issue, is for was) fits the heading and the next paragraph, which explains why his own practice is better. (3) "that susceptible to hypnosis" for "especially suggestible" is the same strength. (4) "state-dependent" is not restored, but the change does not say it restores it and the replaced words did not have it. Linter D9 (follows the source order): accepted. The order is his own (a smaller possible reason, then the larger one), the change is two sentences in an otherwise unchanged section, and the turn from a hedged first reason to a bigger one is a thought-turn that notices something, so T13 and T09 do not apply. Tell rows T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 were judged on the literal draft in its context and none is PRESENT. Looked at closely and found absent: T07, T11 and T19 (the hedges are real thought-turns, and the second sentence carries the claim that the next paragraphs unpack, it does not only announce); T12 and T18 (the two-reason pair is his own, and the second sentence adds to the first, it does not flip it); T20 and T29 (the paragraph ends on his phrase, and the last sentence adds a new consideration, so cutting it would lose a claim); T06 ("trust and precision" is his phrase and is made concrete in the next paragraph); T15 (a recast in a more casual voice, not synonym swaps); C02 (see "when I did that" above); C03 (every first-person fact is in his published guide). Provenance note on ADMISSION.json, not on the draft: its D9 reason calls "One reason might have been" Emulate's own turn, but the_change says it is the writer's fix of Emulate's "One reason was".
